about: Every item in the game (doc 35). weight: lb. price: base price in silver pennies at Common quality (a mark is 10p). stack: how many fit in one inventory stack (1 = each is unique). keeps: days before it spoils. durability: uses before it needs repair. source (raw materials): where it is gathered or bought. Check with python3 tools/item_catalog.py.

items.name: Wheat (measure)
items.desc: A measure of threshed wheat.

items.name: Rye (measure)
items.desc: Dark grain that grows where wheat sulks.

items.name: Barley (measure)
items.desc: Brewers' grain.

items.name: Oats (measure)
items.desc: Porridge for the poor and fodder for horses.

items.name: Flax (bundle)
items.desc: Pulled flax stalks, ready for retting into linen.

items.name: Flaxseed (bag)
items.desc: Pressed for linseed oil.

items.name: Hemp (bundle)
items.desc: Tough fibre for rope, sacking and canvas.

items.name: Straw (bale)
items.desc: Bedding, thatch and hat straw.

items.name: Hay (bale)
items.desc: A horse eats one a day.

items.name: Vegetables (basket)
items.desc: Turnips, onions, cabbage: filler for the stewpot.

items.name: Apples (basket)
items.desc: Cider apples, mostly.

items.name: Grapes (basket)
items.desc: From the golden hills above Ser Ferro.

items.name: Berries (basket)
items.desc: Wild or hedgerow berries; pemmican needs them.

items.name: Milk (jug)
items.desc: Cow or goat milk. Sours in a day.

items.name: Raw wool (fleece)
items.desc: One shearing's fleece, greasy and full of burrs.

items.name: Feathers (bundle)
items.desc: Goose and hen feathers: quills, fletching, stuffing.

items.name: Honey (pot)
items.desc: Food, medicine and mead.

items.name: Beeswax (cake)
items.desc: Fine candles, salves and sealing wax.

items.name: Cattle (head)
items.desc: Led on a rope. A butcher turns one into a great deal.

items.name: Sheep (head)
items.desc: Led on a rope.

items.name: Pig (head)
items.desc: Led, protesting, on a rope.

items.name: Goat (head)
items.desc: Led on a rope; eats the rope.

items.name: Draught horse
items.desc: A heavy horse for carts, wagons, ploughs and mill-gins. Horses are not ridden; no wolf would. Eats a bale of hay or two measures of oats a day.

items.name: Timber (log)
items.desc: A trimmed log, dragged or carted.

items.name: Firewood (bundle)
items.desc: Split wood for hearths and ovens.

items.name: Oak bark (bundle)
items.desc: Ground for tanning liquor.

items.name: Pine resin (lump)
items.desc: For pitch, varnish, incense and ink gum.

items.name: Oak galls (bag)
items.desc: Black dye and iron-gall ink.

items.name: Mushrooms (basket)
items.desc: Good in stew. Mostly.

items.name: Shed antler
items.desc: Found in spring; carved into chews, handles and dice.

items.name: Cooking herbs
items.desc: A bundle of mixed pot herbs.

items.name: Yarrow
items.desc: Stanches bleeding.

items.name: Willow bark
items.desc: Bitter; eases pain and fever.

items.name: Comfrey
items.desc: Knitbone: bruises and breaks.

items.name: Valerian root
items.desc: Smells of old socks; brings sleep.

items.name: Chamomile
items.desc: Calming tea and eyewash.

items.name: Mint
items.desc: Tea and breath.

items.name: Thyme
items.desc: Coughs and the cookpot.

items.name: Garlic
items.desc: Wounds, worms and dinner.

items.name: Wormwood
items.desc: Fleas, worms and the bitterest tea in the world.

items.name: Lavender
items.desc: Scent for soap, oil and the linen chest.

items.name: Rose petals
items.desc: The base of the finest perfumes.

items.name: Woad (bundle)
items.desc: Blue dye.

items.name: Madder root
items.desc: Red dye.

items.name: Weld (bundle)
items.desc: Yellow dye.

items.name: Kermes (pouch)
items.desc: Imported scarlet; the colour of rank.

items.name: Alum (lump)
items.desc: Mordant that fixes dye into cloth.

items.name: Iron ore
items.desc: Red-brown rock, heavy for its size.

items.name: Copper ore
items.desc: Green-streaked rock.

items.name: Tin ore
items.desc: Black tinstone; scarce.

items.name: Lead ore
items.desc: Galena, often with a little silver in it.

items.name: Silver ore
items.desc: Rich ore; guarded.

items.name: Calamine
items.desc: Zinc ore; turns copper into brass.

items.name: Coal (sack)
items.desc: Smoky sea-coal; poor for smithing, fine for lime and salt.

items.name: Building stone (block)
items.desc: Rough-quarried block.

items.name: Marble (block)
items.desc: White Ser Ferro marble.

items.name: Limestone
items.desc: Burnt for lime.

items.name: Clay
items.desc: Potter's and brickmaker's clay.

items.name: Sand
items.desc: For glass and mortar.

items.name: Peat (stack)
items.desc: Cut turf from the Mirelands; slow, smoky fuel.

items.name: Garnet
items.desc: Deep red stone.

items.name: Amber
items.desc: Washed up on the steppe rivers and the coast.

items.name: River pearl
items.desc: Small and grey-lustred.

items.name: Fine gemstone
items.desc: Sapphire or emerald from abroad.

items.name: Jet
items.desc: Black stone for mourning pieces.

items.name: Reeds (bundle)
items.desc: Baskets, thatch and pipe reeds.

items.name: Wood ash (bucket)
items.desc: Every hearth makes it; the chandler buys it for lye.

items.name: Linen rags (bundle)
items.desc: Worn-out linen; the papermaker buys it by the bale.

items.name: Spices (pouch)
items.desc: Pepper and cinnamon from very far away.

items.name: Cloves (pouch)
items.desc: For toothache and perfume.

items.name: Frankincense
items.desc: Church incense.

items.name: Musk (grain)
items.desc: The base note of costly perfume.

items.name: Citrus (basket)
items.desc: Bitter oranges and lemons.

items.name: Silk (ell)
items.desc: Woven silk by the ell.

items.name: Velvet (ell)
items.desc: Silk velvet; nobles and rich merchants.

items.name: Gold (dram)
items.desc: An eighth of an ounce of gold.

items.name: Pipe-weed (pouch)
items.desc: Smoked in a pipe. Fixer lights his with a Gift.

items.name: Charcoal (sack)
items.desc: Clean, hot fuel for forges, crucibles and braziers.

items.name: Potash
items.desc: Leached and boiled ash; glass flux.

items.name: Lye (crock)
items.desc: Caustic ash-water for soap.

items.name: Pitch (pot)
items.desc: Boiled resin and tar: caulking, waterproofing, torches.

items.name: Lampblack
items.desc: Soot scraped from smoking lamps; printing ink.

items.name: Tallow (cake)
items.desc: Rendered animal fat.

items.name: Fat scraps
items.desc: Raw suet and trimmings from butchery.

items.name: Linseed oil (flask)
items.desc: Pressed from flaxseed: paint, oilcloth, ink, lamps.

items.name: Aqua vitae (flask)
items.desc: Distilled spirit; medicine base, perfume base, strong drink.

items.name: Salt (sack)
items.desc: Food keeps because of it. A town without salt goes hungry in winter.

items.name: Malt (measure)
items.desc: Sprouted, kilned barley.

items.name: Flour (measure)
items.desc: Ground at the mill.

items.name: Hide
items.desc: A raw cattle or deer hide. Rots if not tanned.

items.name: Sheepskin
items.desc: Wool-on skin for linings.

items.name: Bones (bundle)
items.desc: Broth, glue, charms and dice.

items.name: Gut (coil)
items.desc: Cleaned gut: sausage skins, bowstrings, stitching thread.

items.name: Sinew (bundle)
items.desc: Dried tendon; the best crossbow cord.

items.name: Horn
items.desc: Lantern panes, combs, hartshorn salts.

items.name: Bristles (bundle)
items.desc: Pig bristle for brushes.

items.name: Hide glue (pot)
items.desc: Boiled from scraps and bones; holds furniture and bows together.

items.name: Rawhide
items.desc: Scraped and dried, untanned: stiff, strong, cheap.

items.name: Leather (side)
items.desc: Bark-tanned leather.

items.name: Boiled leather (plate)
items.desc: Leather boiled in wax and moulded: cuir bouilli.

items.name: Parchment (sheet)
items.desc: Limed and stretched skin. Lasts forever; deeds are written on it.

items.name: Sheepskin lining
items.desc: Trimmed sheepskin ready to sew into a mantle or wraps.

items.name: Wool yarn (skein)
items.desc: Spun on a paw-treadled wheel.

items.name: Linen yarn (skein)
items.desc: Retted, scutched and spun flax.

items.name: Hemp yarn (skein)
items.desc: Coarse yarn for cord, rope and canvas.

items.name: Wool cloth (ell)
items.desc: Fulled woollen cloth.

items.name: Linen (ell)
items.desc: Plain-woven linen.

items.name: Canvas (ell)
items.desc: Heavy hemp cloth: sails, sacks, tents.

items.name: Felt (piece)
items.desc: Wool matted with soap and hot water.

items.name: Dyed wool cloth (ell)
items.desc: Wool cloth dyed blue, red, yellow, black or green; the colour is chosen when dyed.

items.name: Scarlet cloth (ell)
items.desc: Kermes-dyed wool. Only the rich wear true scarlet.

items.name: Oilcloth (ell)
items.desc: Canvas soaked in linseed oil: sheds rain.

items.name: Rope (coil, 50 ft)
items.desc: Every well, ship, mine, crane and cart needs it.

items.name: Cord (hank)
items.desc: Twisted hemp cord.

items.name: Candle wick (hank)
items.desc: Braided linen wick.

items.name: Iron bloom
items.desc: Spongy iron straight from the smelter, full of slag.

items.name: Wrought iron (bar)
items.desc: Hammered bloom: nails, fittings, hoops, cheap blades.

items.name: Steel (bar)
items.desc: Carburised and folded iron; keeps an edge.

items.name: Iron scale
items.desc: Flakes from the anvil; dissolved for ink and black dye.

items.name: Copper (bar)
items.desc: Smelted copper.

items.name: Tin (bar)
items.desc: Smelted tin.

items.name: Lead (bar)
items.desc: Smelted lead: pipes, roofing, type metal.

items.name: Silver (dram)
items.desc: An eighth-ounce of refined silver, the metal of pennies.

items.name: Bronze (bar)
items.desc: Copper and tin: bells, fittings, mortars, gears.

items.name: Brass (bar)
items.desc: Copper and calamine: buckles, fittings, cheap jewellery.

items.name: Pewter (bar)
items.desc: Tin and lead: tableware.

items.name: Type metal (bar)
items.desc: Lead and tin that casts sharp and cools fast.

items.name: Iron wire (coil)
items.desc: Drawn through a plate: snares, mail rings, pins.

items.name: Brass wire (coil)
items.desc: Jewellery, spectacles, pins.

items.name: Brass sheet
items.desc: Hammered thin: lanterns, trumpets, scales.

items.name: Tinplate
items.desc: Tinned iron sheet: lanterns, cups.

items.name: Rivets (bag)
items.desc: Iron rivets for brigandine and buckles.

items.name: Mail rings (bag)
items.desc: Riveted iron rings, a few thousand to the bag.

items.name: Buckles (set)
items.desc: Brass or iron buckles and rings for harness.

items.name: Needles (paper of 10)
items.desc: Steel needles.

items.name: Planks (bundle)
items.desc: Sawn boards.

items.name: Beam
items.desc: A squared beam for roofs, frames and bridges.

items.name: Barrel staves (bundle)
items.desc: Riven and shaved oak staves.

items.name: Iron hoops (set)
items.desc: Hoops for one barrel.

items.name: Quicklime (sack)
items.desc: Burnt limestone: mortar, plaster, tanning.

items.name: Mortar (tub)
items.desc: Lime and sand.

items.name: Plaster (tub)
items.desc: Lime plaster for the white walls of Ridgemere and Ser Ferro.

items.name: Dressed marble
items.desc: Ser Ferro's steps, columns and palace floors.

items.name: Dressed stone
items.desc: Squared and faced: walls, bridges, steps.

items.name: Bricks (hod of 20)
items.desc: Kiln-fired.

items.name: Roof tiles (stack of 20)
items.desc: The red tiles of Ser Ferro.

items.name: Glass (lump)
items.desc: Raw glass from the furnace.

items.name: Window glass (pane)
items.desc: Small crown-glass panes set in lead.

items.name: Glass vials (×6)
items.desc: For perfume and medicine.

items.name: Ground lens
items.desc: A lens ground true on the wheel.

items.name: Nails (bag of 50)
items.desc: Every building, crate and cart eats them.

items.name: Iron fittings (set)
items.desc: Hinges, straps and a mouth-pull latch for one door or chest.

items.name: Chain (fathom)
items.desc: Wrought links: wells, gates, ships, mines.

items.name: Cart wheel
items.desc: Spoked, iron-tyred.

items.name: Axle
items.desc: Iron-shod oak axle.

items.name: Wooden gears (set)
items.desc: Cogs and lantern-pinions for mills, windlasses and presses.

items.name: Millstone
items.desc: A pair of dressed stones. Moved by wagon and four wolves.

items.name: Crossbow prod
items.desc: A spring-steel bow for an emplacement crossbow. Few smiths can make one.

items.name: Windlass
items.desc: A paw-cranked winch that spans an emplacement crossbow.

items.name: Crossbow cable
items.desc: Twisted sinew and hemp.

items.name: Printing ink (pot)
items.desc: Lampblack ground into boiled linseed oil.

items.name: Case of type
items.desc: A full fount of cast letters with its case. The press is useless without it.

items.name: Fang knife
items.desc: A short steel blade on a bit, edge forward. Quick, cheap, easy to hide in a sling.

items.name: Iron bit-sword
items.desc: A wrought-iron blade: heavier, duller and cheaper than steel. Bends rather than breaks.

items.name: Bit-sword
items.desc: The common steel sidearm: a padded bit across the back teeth, a lip guard, and a blade out of the side of the mouth.

items.name: Needle rapier
items.desc: A long, light thrusting blade; a duellist's and a noble's weapon.

items.name: Hook cleaver

weapon.special: Disarm: on a hit, 25% chance to knock the target's mouth weapon loose.

items.desc: A heavy chopping blade with a back hook for tearing another wolf's weapon away.

items.name: Bit-axe
items.desc: A bearded axe head on a short haft gripped by a bit. Also a woodsman's tool.

items.name: War pick
items.desc: A narrow steel beak that punches through mail and plate.

items.name: Weighted cudgel

weapon.special: Nonlethal: a wolf it brings to 0 health is Downed, never killed.

items.desc: A lead-cored club on a bit. The watch carries one to bring wolves in alive.

items.name: Flanged mace

weapon.special: Mail's extra protection against cuts does not apply.

items.desc: A steel-flanged head on a bit-haft. Mail does not help much against it.

items.name: Mouth flail

weapon.special: On a miss, 10% chance to hit the wielder for half damage.

items.desc: A spiked ball on a short chain from a bit, swung with a toss of the head.

items.name: Leather cosh

weapon.special: From behind or unseen: the target loses its next turn (stunned).

items.desc: A sand-filled leather sap. Thieves and bouncers.

items.name: Steel fang caps

weapon.special: Adds +6 to Bite and 1 pierce. Cannot be knocked loose.

items.desc: Sheaths over the canines. Worn in the mouth; Bite stays your attack and hits harder.

items.name: Steel claw caps

weapon.special: Rake: a paw attack, usable while something is held in the mouth.

items.desc: Steel sheaths over the foreclaws. Worn on the paws: unlocks a forepaw rake.

items.name: Wall crossbow (dismantled)
items.desc: A light emplacement crossbow on a timber trestle. Moved by handcart; two wolves set it up in 10 minutes, on a wall, tower or prepared spot. Once set up it becomes a station that one wolf aims with a mouth tiller and fires with a bite cord; spanning it takes a paw-cranked windlass.

items.name: Siege crossbow (dismantled)

siege.special: Knocks down: the target loses its next move.

items.desc: A great crossbow like a ballista, in pieces. Needs a wagon and a horse to move and a crew of three and an hour to set up. Two crew span and fire it; its bolt can kill outright and knocks wolves flat.

items.name: Emplacement bolts (×10)
items.desc: Iron-headed bolts for a wall crossbow.

items.name: Siege bolts (×4)
items.desc: Spear-sized bolts for a siege crossbow.

items.name: Quilted vest
items.desc: Layers of linen stitched over wool. Warm, and a start.

items.name: Leather barding
items.desc: A fitted leather coat over back, ribs and chest.

items.name: Boiled-leather barding
items.desc: Cuir bouilli plates moulded to the ribs and spine.

items.name: Brigandine coat
items.desc: Small steel plates riveted inside a cloth coat; the rivet heads make a pattern only rich guards can afford to show.

items.name: Mail coat
items.desc: Riveted mail over a padded lining. Jingles.

items.name: Leather gorget
items.desc: A stiff leather throat guard. The cheapest armour that matters most.

items.name: Spiked collar
items.special: A Bite on the wearer's throat deals 4 damage to the biter.
items.desc: A broad collar set with iron spikes. A wolf that bites the throat pays for it.

items.name: Mail neck guard
items.desc: A mail curtain hung from a helm or collar.

items.name: Steel gorget
items.desc: A steel throat plate, often engraved; an officer's piece.

items.name: Linen neckerchief
items.desc: A square of linen knotted at the throat; a working wolf's scarf.

items.name: Wool scarf
items.desc: Wound twice round the neck against the wind.

items.name: Silk scarf
items.desc: Bright silk tied loose under the ruff; for being seen.

items.name: Leather neck wrap
items.desc: A soft leather band laced round the throat; better than fur alone.

items.name: Leather cap with ear slits
items.desc: A stiff cap that leaves the ears free.

items.name: Kettle helm
items.desc: A brimmed steel helm with ear slits; the watch's helmet. Dulls hearing a little.

items.name: Chamfron
items.desc: A brow-and-muzzle plate. Can be worn with fang caps.

items.name: Leg guards and paw boots
items.special: Counts as paw boots for footing.
items.desc: Leather greaves laced over paw boots.

items.name: Splinted greaves
items.desc: Steel splints riveted to leather leg guards.

items.name: Ear-slit felt cap
items.desc: The everyday working wolf's cap.

items.name: Wide straw sun hat
items.desc: Plaited straw with a broad brim and ear holes; farmers.

items.name: Wool hood with ear sleeves
items.desc: Knitted sleeves keep the ears warm in winter.

items.name: Oilcloth rain hat
items.desc: Sailors' and couriers' hat; Ridgemere lives in them.

items.name: Chaperon
items.desc: A draped hood-hat in guild or house colours; town fashion.

items.name: Scholar's coif
items.desc: A close linen cap: clerks, scribes, physicians.

items.name: Velvet beret with feather
items.desc: Merchants and nobles; the plume is dyed to the house.

items.name: Mourning veil-hat
items.desc: Black gauze worn after a death in the family.

items.name: Cleric's cap
items.desc: Issued by the church to its own.

items.name: Sheepskin hat
items.desc: Fleece-lined with ear sleeves: the northern moor's hat.

items.name: Patched wrap
items.desc: Rags stitched together. The poorest wolves.

items.name: Plain wool shawl
items.desc: The common wolf's shawl; warm.

items.name: Linen summer shawl
items.desc: Light; keeps off sun and flies.

items.name: Oiled rain cape
items.desc: Sheds rain and wet snow.

items.name: Fur-lined winter mantle
items.desc: Wool over sheepskin; the warmest thing a wolf can wear.

items.name: Fringed silk shawl
items.desc: Imported silk; nobility and festivals.

items.name: House-colour shawl
items.desc: Livery of a noble house or the watch.

items.name: Embroidered festival shawl
items.desc: Worn on festival days; every family has its own pattern.

items.name: Black mourning shawl
items.desc: Oak-gall black wool.

items.name: Scarlet mantle
items.desc: True kermes scarlet: magistrates, guildmasters, lords.

items.name: Plain strap harness
items.desc: Everyone's first harness.

items.name: Padded work harness
items.special: Can pull a handcart or sled.
items.desc: A padded chest plate; pulls a handcart or sled.

items.name: Courier harness
items.special: Carries a document tube without using a loop.
items.desc: Light, with a built-in document tube.

items.name: Guard harness
items.special: Sheath draw in a fight is free.
items.desc: Reinforced, with a quick-draw sheath loop.

items.name: Pack harness
items.desc: A frame for panniers and bundles.

items.name: Draught harness
items.special: Pulls a handcart or sled at a full load.
items.desc: Collar-pad and traces for pulling a laden cart or sled. Nothing else hangs on it.

items.name: Tooled dress harness
items.desc: Tooled leather with brass fittings, for occasions.

items.name: Silver-fitted harness
items.desc: Engraved silver fittings and a House crest.

items.name: Harness sheath
items.desc: Holds one mouth weapon at the shoulder, so the mouth is free.

items.name: Harness pouch
items.desc: Holds 3 lb: coins, a fire kit, a letter.

items.name: Panniers (pair)
items.desc: Saddlebags for a wolf. Take two loops; hold 30 lb.

items.name: Lantern hook
items.desc: A sprung iron hook for a harness lantern.

items.name: Tool roll
items.desc: A leather roll for a crafter's small tools.

items.name: Sling bag
items.desc: Worn across the body; holds 10 lb.

items.name: Scabbard sling
items.desc: Sheathes one weapon across the back without a harness.

items.name: Water skin
items.desc: On a sling. Full, it weighs 3 lb more.

items.name: Document tube sling
items.desc: Keeps letters and maps dry.

items.name: Bandolier
items.desc: Six vials or small tools in loops.

items.name: Gatherer's sling basket
items.desc: Herbs and mushrooms; gathering is faster.

items.name: Linen paw wraps
items.desc: Everyday; protects cracked pads.

items.name: Felted winter wraps
items.desc: Warmth and grip on snow and ice.

items.name: Leather paw boots
items.desc: Rock, gravel and long roads.

items.name: Hobnailed travel boots
items.desc: Fast on roads; loud on stone.

items.name: Oiled marsh wraps
items.desc: Mud and wet ground.

items.name: Soft-soled sneak wraps
items.desc: Felt soles: quieter footfalls. Thieves' gear.

items.name: Silk dancing wraps
items.desc: Court and festivals.

items.name: Leather paw bindings
items.desc: Thongs of leather bound criss-cross up each leg; a sure grip on stone.

items.name: Fleece-lined boots
items.desc: Sheepskin inside leather; the north's winter boots.

items.name: Bone fur clip
items.desc: Folk craft; anyone can carve one.

items.name: Brass fur clip
items.desc: The common wolf's adornment.

items.name: Silver fur clip
items.desc: Clipped into the ruff, the cheek fur or the tail.

items.name: Gold fur clip
items.desc: Rich and quietly heavy.

items.name: Gem-set fur clip
items.desc: Silver set with a garnet, amber, pearl or jet; the stone is chosen when made.

items.name: Jewelled gold clip
items.desc: Gold set with a fine stone. A noble's piece.

items.name: Glass ruff beads (string)
items.desc: Bright glass beads braided into the ruff.

items.name: Bone ruff beads (string)
items.desc: Carved bone beads.

items.name: Amber ruff beads (string)
items.desc: Honey-coloured amber.

items.name: Silver ruff beads (string)
items.desc: Small silver beads that click softly.

items.name: Brass ear cuff
items.desc: Clamps round the ear; no piercing.

items.name: Silver ear cuff
items.desc: Engraved silver round the ear.

items.name: Pierced ear ring
items.desc: Brass or silver; piercing is done by a healer or a jeweler.

items.name: Brass tail ring
items.desc: Swings with the tail, so mood shows more.

items.name: Silver tail ring
items.desc: Swings with the tail, so mood shows more.

items.name: Gold tail ring
items.desc: A heavy gold band near the tail's root.

items.name: Ribbon tail clasp
items.desc: Silk ribbon on a small clasp.

items.name: Dangling charm
items.desc: A small cast token hung from a clip or a harness loop.

items.name: Little bells
items.desc: Loud on purpose: pups, dancers, festivals.

items.name: Scent locket

items.name: Fang charm
items.desc: A tooth on a cord: a luck token, or a trophy.

items.name: Jet mourning clip
items.desc: Polished jet set in pewter.

items.name: Paired betrothal clips

items.desc: Made as a pair; each partner wears one.

items.name: Gilded claw caps
items.desc: Decorative gilt over the claws; worn with any paw wear.

items.desc: A House's crest in silver. Issued, never sold; wearing one you weren't given is impersonation.

items.desc: A Chapter's mark. Issued by the Chapter.

items.name: Ribbon collar
items.desc: A dyed ribbon tied at the throat.

items.name: Tooled leather collar
items.desc: Tooled leather with a brass buckle.

items.name: Brass-studded collar
items.desc: Leather set with polished brass studs.

items.name: Silver chain collar
items.desc: Fine silver links worn loose in the ruff.

items.name: Gold filigree collar
items.desc: Gold wirework over the throat ruff; worth a house in the Sump.

items.name: Jewelled collar
